speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where your wrist pain is located and what specific movements make it difficult for you to move your hand.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis. The patient's history of falling on her outstretched hand likely caused trauma to the first dorsal compartment, leading to tendonitis exacerbated by repetitive lifting (holding an infant). The radiation of pain to the elbow suggests possible concomitant lateral epicondylitis or referred pain from the wrist pathology, but the primary issue is the tendonitis. I will recommend imaging to confirm the extent of the inflammation and rule out other pathologies. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hand_ultrasound.
